issues.text: Summary line 3 says every Compose service had its own address, but section 4 of this lesson (and docker-compose.yml@stage-2 L48) says `web` has no address of its own: it uses `network_mode: "service:lab"` and shares lab's 172.28.0.12. The summary contradicts the lesson's own example.
issues.quote: as each Compose service had its own address.
issues.fix: Change to "as `db` and `api` each had their own address in Compose." (same change in vi.md).

issues.text: New clause in the Pod IP bullet: I do not know which Pods are "Kubernetes' own Pods". The lesson never says Kubernetes runs any Pods of its own. I can skip it, because section 4 says every Pod I create gets its own IP, but I still stopped here.
issues.quote: while a few of Kubernetes' own Pods use their node's address instead.
issues.fix: Name them in a few words, e.g. "a few Pods that run parts of the control plane use their node's address instead", or drop the clause and keep "each Pod you create gets its own".

issues.text: On first read the sentence says the comment line itself "sends this file to the cluster". I had to re-read it to see that the next lesson does the sending.
issues.quote: Two comment lines point ahead: `# lesson: k8s.l1.manifests-and-kubectl-apply`, the next lesson, sends this file to the cluster, and the namespace line can be ignored until the lesson on namespaces.
issues.fix: Reword: "Two comment lines point ahead: `# lesson: k8s.l1.manifests-and-kubectl-apply` names the next lesson, which sends this file to the cluster, and the namespace line can be ignored until the lesson on namespaces."

issues.text: The last paragraph opens with "So", but it does not follow from the paragraph before it, which is about `network_mode`. I looked back for the reason and did not find one.
issues.quote: So most Pods hold one container, like `web`.
issues.fix: Drop "So": "Most Pods hold one container, like `web`."
